subject: maths

concepts.title: Closure Property of Addition and Subtraction
concepts.definition: Integers are closed under addition and subtraction, meaning the sum or difference of any two integers is always an integer.
concepts.formula: a + b = integer; a - b = integer
concepts.key_idea: The result of adding or subtracting integers never leaves the set of integers.
question_patterns: Is the sum of these integers an integer?
Verify closure property for the following pair
What is the result of subtracting these two integers?
Check if integers are closed under subtraction

solution_steps.explain: Add or subtract the given integers a and b.
Confirm if the resulting value belongs to the set of integers.

concepts.title: Commutative Property of Addition
concepts.definition: The sum of two integers remains the same regardless of the order in which they are added.
concepts.key_idea: Order does not affect the result in integer addition.
question_patterns: Verify the commutative property for addition
Does changing the order of addition change the sum?
Calculate the sum in two different orders

solution_steps.explain: Add the first integer to the second.
Add the second integer to the first.

concepts.title: Associative Property of Addition
concepts.definition: When adding three integers, the grouping of the numbers does not change the final sum.
concepts.key_idea: Grouping of terms is flexible in integer addition.
question_patterns: Verify the associative property for the given integers
Group the integers differently and find the sum
Show that (a+b)+c equals a+(b+c)
Find the missing value using associativity

solution_steps.explain: Add a and b first, then add c.
Add b and c first, then add a.

concepts.title: Additive Identity
concepts.definition: Zero is the additive identity for integers because adding zero to any integer results in that same integer.
concepts.key_idea: Adding zero preserves the identity of the integer.
question_patterns: What is the additive identity of integers?
Find the sum of an integer and zero
Identify the property: -23 + 0 = -23
What must be added to an integer to get the same value?

solution_steps.explain: Add 0 to the given integer val_a.

concepts.title: Multiplication of Unlike Signed Integers
concepts.definition: The product of a positive integer and a negative integer is a negative integer, found by multiplying their absolute values and adding a minus sign.
concepts.key_idea: Positive times negative always equals negative.
question_patterns: Multiply a positive and a negative integer
Find the product of 6 and -19
Calculate the result of multiplying unlike signs
What is the sign of the product of 15 and -16?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers.
Since signs are different, the product is negative.

concepts.title: Multiplication of Two Negative Integers
concepts.definition: Multiplying two negative integers results in a positive integer product.
concepts.key_idea: Negative times negative always equals positive.
question_patterns: Find the product of two negative integers
Calculate (-21) times (-30)
What is the result of multiplying -10 and -12?
Verify that the product of two negatives is positive

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the absolute values of the two negative integers.

concepts.title: Multiplicative Identity
concepts.definition: The integer 1 is the multiplicative identity for integers, as any integer multiplied by 1 remains unchanged.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying by 1 does not change the value.
question_patterns: What is the multiplicative identity for integers?
Multiply an integer by 1
Identify the property: (-3) * 1 = -3
Find the product of -4 and 1

concepts.title: Distributive Property
concepts.definition: Multiplication distributes over addition and subtraction, meaning a(b + c) = ab + ac.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying a sum is equal to the sum of the individual products.
question_patterns: Verify the distributive property
Solve using distributive property: 18 * [7 + (-3)]
Show that a(b-c) = ab - ac
Calculate the product using distributivity

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the outer integer by the first inner integer.
Multiply the outer integer by the second inner integer.

concepts.title: Division of Integers
concepts.definition: Division of integers follows sign rules similar to multiplication: unlike signs result in a negative quotient, and like signs result in a positive quotient.
concepts.key_idea: Sign of the quotient depends on the signs of the dividend and divisor.
question_patterns: Divide a negative integer by a positive one
Find the quotient of (-36) and (-9)
Calculate 50 divided by -5
What is the result of dividing -100 by 5?

solution_steps.explain: Divide the absolute values of the numbers.
If signs were different, result is negative; if same, result is positive.

concepts.title: Properties of Division
concepts.definition: Division is not commutative or associative for integers; division by zero is undefined, and division by 1 returns the same integer.
concepts.key_idea: Division has specific constraints and lacks commutativity.
question_patterns: Is division commutative for integers?
What is the result of dividing an integer by 1?
Evaluate 0 divided by -12
Check if (a/b)/c equals a/(b/c)

solution_steps.explain: Divide the integer by the divisor (1 or 0).
State if the result is the integer itself or undefined.

Subtract correct marks from total score.
